principles: The rule is advisory process discipline written into truth-source docs — not a CLI gate, not auto-enforced
Scope narrowly to process-framework stories; ordinary business stories must not inherit a combination-review burden
The rule text must be actionable — name the concrete inspection checklist, cite the originating incident (B-8db9)
drivers: B-8db9 proved single-story review structurally misses cross-story interaction defects
The lesson currently lives only in conversation and will be lost without a doc
Future parallel process-framework stories carry the same combination-bypass risk

options.name: A: Write the rule into both CLAUDE.md and decisions/story-lifecycle.md
pros: CLAUDE.md is what agents read every session — maximum visibility
story-lifecycle.md is the lifecycle truth source — authoritative home
Cross-referenced so neither copy drifts silently
cons: Two files to keep in sync; risk of divergence over time

options.name: B: Write only into CLAUDE.md
pros: Single file, no sync risk, agents see it every session
cons: story-lifecycle.md is the lifecycle truth source — a lifecycle rule absent there is a documentation gap
Future lifecycle-doc readers miss the rule

options.name: C: Write only into decisions/story-lifecycle.md
cons: Agents read CLAUDE.md every session but not necessarily story-lifecycle.md — low operational visibility for the people who must act on it

chosen: A: Write the rule into both CLAUDE.md and decisions/story-lifecycle.md
rationale: Choose A because the rule needs both operational visibility (CLAUDE.md, read every session by every agent) and truth-source authority (story-lifecycle.md, where lifecycle rules formally live). Reject B because omitting it from the lifecycle truth source leaves a documentation gap — a lifecycle rule that is not in the lifecycle doc. Reject C because agents do not read story-lifecycle.md every session, so the people who must run the combination review would not see it. The sync risk of A is mitigated by keeping the CLAUDE.md copy short and pointing to story-lifecycle.md as the canonical detailed version.

preMortem.scenario: The rule is so broadly worded that every parallel story (including ordinary business stories) triggers a combination review, creating review fatigue
preMortem.trigger: The doc text omits or vaguely defines what counts as a process-framework story
preMortem.consequence: Teams either drown in unnecessary combination reviews or start ignoring the rule entirely
preMortem.mitigation: The rule text MUST enumerate the concrete trigger set — classifier / gate policy / command entry guards / auto-commit / DONE merge semantics — and explicitly state ordinary business stories are out of scope. Verification: grep the doc for the literal scope sentence.

preMortem.scenario: The CLAUDE.md copy and the story-lifecycle.md copy drift apart over time
preMortem.trigger: A future edit updates one file but not the other
preMortem.consequence: Two contradictory versions of the rule; readers do not know which is canonical
preMortem.mitigation: CLAUDE.md carries a short summary that explicitly points to docs/requirements/decisions/story-lifecycle.md as the canonical detailed version. Only the canonical copy carries the full checklist. Verification: the CLAUDE.md copy contains a see-also pointer to story-lifecycle.md.

preMortem.scenario: The rule is written as vague prose with no actionable checklist, so a combination review degrades to a rubber-stamp
preMortem.trigger: The doc says run a combination review but does not say what to inspect
preMortem.consequence: Reviewers do a cursory pass and miss exactly the kind of cross-story bypass B-8db9 had
preMortem.mitigation: The rule MUST include the concrete inspection checklist: classification priority order, gate policy table, command entry rejection, auto-commit/dirty state, DONE merge semantics. Verification: the doc section contains an enumerated checklist, not just a directive sentence.
